title: Quasi-compact open locus of closed embeddings from a finite locally free source
statement: Let $P$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $D\to P$ be finite locally free [def-pc-finite-locally-free], let $X\to P$ be affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism] and of finite presentation, and let $f:D\to X$ be a $P$-morphism. Finite presentation means locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. There is a quasi-compact open immersion $V\hookrightarrow P$ [def-weil-open-immersion] such that for every scheme $T$ and morphism $t:T\to P$, $t$ factors through $V$ if and only if the base change $f_T:D\times_PT\to X\times_PT$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-pc-fibre-product]. Equivalently, $|V|$ is the set of $p\in P$ where $f_{\kappa(p)}$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-residue-field]. This description commutes with arbitrary base change on $P$. The rank-zero source, empty bases, and nonreduced bases are allowed; no Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Lemma 2.3.4, proof, printed p.70, open monicity locus. The stated general finite-source version and quasi-compactness over arbitrary rings are the finite-coordinate/minor formulation of this input, agent-stated; source proof uses a Noetherian reduction. Read online; WANTED locally as literature/conrad-reductive-group-schemes.pdf.

proof.text: Put $E=(D\to P)_*\mathcal O_D$. By [def-pc-finite-locally-free] and [lem-sc-finite-pushforward-locally-free], $E$ is locally free of finite, locally varying rank. Choose affine opens $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ trivializing $E$. The definition [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] of finiteness makes $D_U$ affine, and [pqf-def-affine-morphism] makes $X_U$ affine; write $D_U=\operatorname{Spec}B$, $X_U=\operatorname{Spec}C$ using [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Here $B$ is free of rank $n$ over $A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation], $C=A[x_1,\ldots,x_m]/(r_1,\ldots,r_l)$ for finite $m,l$. The given map is an $A$-algebra map $\phi:C\to B$. Write $b_i=\phi(x_i)$. If $n=0$, then $B=0$ and every scalar extension of $\phi$ is surjective; set the local locus equal to $U$. For the next five steps assume $n>0$.

source.place: 02KB (lemma-finite-flat); 01TQ (lemma-locally-finite-presentation-characterize); affine setup for the finite-coordinate argument

proof.text: For each $i$, apply [lem-weil-cayley-hamilton-free-module] to the $A$-linear endomorphism $z\mapsto b_i z$ of $B$. Evaluating its monic degree-$n$ characteristic-polynomial relation at $1_B$ gives $b_i^n=-\sum_{j<n}a_{ij}b_i^j$ for coefficients $a_{ij}\in A$. Thus any monomial with some exponent $e_i\ge n$ is a sum of monomials of strictly smaller total degree, by substituting this relation after multiplying it by $b_i^{e_i-n}\prod_{h\ne i}b_h^{e_h}$. Induction on total degree shows that $\operatorname{im}\phi$ is the $A$-linear span of the finite list $w_e=\prod_i b_i^{e_i}$ with $0\le e_i<n$. The converse inclusion holds because each $w_e$ is the image of $\prod_i x_i^{e_i}$. The empty product when $m=0$ is $1_B$. This is direct polynomial reduction, with no claim that a submodule of a finite module must be finite.

source.place: 00DX (lemma-charpoly): apply the matrix relation to multiplication by each image generator, then reduce monomials

proof.text: Let $N$ be the length of the list $(w_e)$, let $H:A^{\oplus N}\to B$ send the basis vector indexed by $e$ to $w_e$, and set $Q=B/\operatorname{im}H$. For every $A$-algebra $R$, [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact] identifies $Q\otimes_A R$ with the cokernel of $H_R:R^{\oplus N}\to B\otimes_A R$. The image of $\phi_R:C\otimes_A R\to B\otimes_A R$ is exactly the $R$-span of $w_e\otimes1$: each pure tensor maps to $\phi(c)\otimes r$, and Step 2 expresses $\phi(c)$ as an $A$-linear combination of the $w_e$; conversely $w_e\otimes r$ is the image of $(\prod_i x_i^{e_i})\otimes r$. Consequently $\phi_R$ is surjective if and only if $Q\otimes_A R=0$. No tensor-product injection or flatness of $R$ is used.

source.place: 00DF (lemma-tensor-product-exact): cokernel of the finite monomial matrix after arbitrary scalar extension

proof.text: The quotient $Q$ is generated by the images of an $A$-basis of $B$, so $\widetilde Q$ is finite type and quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections]: the same finite generating family generates after each localization. Apply [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-generate-locally] with $\mathcal F=\widetilde Q$ and $r=0$. It supplies an open subscheme $W_U\subseteq U$ such that $h:T\to U$ factors through $W_U$ exactly when $h^*\widetilde Q=0$ (being locally generated by zero sections means zero). For an affine test $T=\operatorname{Spec}R$, [lem-trf-fitting-sheaf-arbitrary-pullback] identifies that pullback with $\widetilde{R\otimes_A Q}$. It vanishes exactly when $R\otimes_A Q=0$, since its global sections are that module by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections] at $D(1)$. Interchanging the two tensor factors, Step 3 therefore gives $h$ factors through $W_U$ if and only if $\phi_R$ is surjective.

Write $M$ for the $n\times N$ matrix of $H$ in the chosen basis of $B$. By [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-sheaf-affine-sections], the ideal $J=\operatorname{Fit}_0(\widetilde Q)(U)$ is generated by the determinants of all $n$ rows from $\ker(A^{\oplus n}\twoheadrightarrow Q)=\operatorname{im}M$. It is already generated by the finite list of determinants $\det(M_{e_1},\ldots,M_{e_n})$, where each $M_e$ is a column of $M$ and repetitions are allowed. Indeed write each selected kernel vector as $z_i=\sum_e c_{ie}M_e$; substituting in the Leibniz formula [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant] and distributing the finite products gives $\det(z_1,\ldots,z_n)=\sum_{e_1,\ldots,e_n}(\prod_i c_{ie_i})\det(M_{e_1},\ldots,M_{e_n})$. Conversely each displayed column is in the kernel; the row convention gives the same determinant by transposing the Leibniz sum. Hence $W_U=\bigcup_\delta D(\delta)$ for this finite determinant list, by the stalk criterion of [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-generate-locally]. No basis of the image module or finite generation of an arbitrary kernel is assumed.

source.place: 07Z8 (lemma-fitting-ideal), presentation matrix description; 07ZA (lemma-fitting-ideal-basics)(4), finite generation by minors, with the finite expansion written out

proof.text: Each $D(\delta)$ is homeomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec}A_\delta$ by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open], and this spectrum is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact]. A finite union of quasi-compact subspaces is quasi-compact: restrict any open cover to each subspace and take the union of its finitely many finite subcovers. Thus $W_U$ is quasi-compact, including when the determinant list is empty. In rank zero $W_U=U$ is quasi-compact by the same spectrum lemma.

For every affine test $\operatorname{Spec}R\to U$, [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identifies the base-changed map $f_R$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(\phi_R)$, since both its projection composites are the maps induced by the tensor inclusions. By the affine criterion of [def-weil-closed-immersion], it is a closed immersion exactly when $\phi_R$ is surjective. Steps 3-4 (and Step 1 in rank zero) prove the required equivalence on affine tests. In particular $p\in W_U$ if and only if $f_{\kappa(p)}$ is a closed immersion. This intrinsic condition shows that the opens $W_U$ coincide on overlaps. Their union is an open subset $V$ of $P$, and [def-weil-open-immersion] equips it with the restricted structure sheaf and its open immersion into $P$.

source.place: 01I4 (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes), 01JQ (lemma-fibre-product-affines); morphisms.tex 01QO (lemma-closed-immersion); intrinsic gluing of the opens

proof.text: To check that $V\hookrightarrow P$ is quasi-compact, take any affine open $A_0\subseteq P$. Refine the local trivializations of $E|_{A_0}$ by principal opens of $A_0$, using the basis clause of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open]. By quasi-compactness of $A_0$ from [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact], finitely many such principal opens cover $A_0$. Each selected principal open is quasi-compact by Step 6's topology argument. Apply [lem-pqf-finite-affine-cover-qc-open] to obtain a finite affine open cover of each one. The resulting finite family covers $A_0$ and trivializes $E$, so Steps 1-7 apply on each member, with its own rank and finite generator list. The intrinsic fibre criterion in Step 7 identifies its constructed locus with $V$ intersected with that chart. Step 6 makes each intersection quasi-compact. Their finite union $V\cap A_0$ is quasi-compact by the open-cover argument in Step 6. This is exactly quasi-compactness of the immersion in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. This is a statement relative to $P$ and does not require $P$ itself to be quasi-compact.

source.place: 00E0 (lemma-Zariski-topology), basic-open basis; 00E4 (lemma-standard-open); 00E8 (lemma-quasi-compact); finite principal refinement on each affine base

proof.text: For arbitrary $t:T\to P$, cover $T$ by affine opens $T_a$ mapping into some chart $U$. Factoring through the open subscheme $V$ is equivalent to factoring locally through its restrictions $W_U$, by [def-weil-open-immersion]. Step 7 says this is equivalent to each $f_{T_a}$ being a closed immersion. These tests imply that $f_T$ is a closed immersion by the topological and sheaf definition [def-weil-closed-immersion]: the inverse images in $X_T$ of the $T_a$ are an open cover; the image of $D_T$ is closed on each of them, hence closed globally; the map is injective and a homeomorphism to its image because these assertions hold on that cover; and surjectivity of the structure-sheaf map is local on that cover. Conversely a closed immersion restricts to one on every target open by the same definition. This proves the equivalence for every $T$, as well as the stated residue-field description.

source.place: 01QO (lemma-closed-immersion), affine-local description; explicit local-to-global check from the definition

proof.text: Finally let $P'\to P$ be arbitrary. Give the inverse-image open subset $V'\subseteq P'$ its restricted structure sheaf [def-weil-open-immersion]. A morphism $T\to P'$ factors through $V'$ if and only if its composite to $P$ factors through $V$. By Step 9 this is equivalent to $f_T$ being a closed immersion. The universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies this $f_T$ with the base change to $T$ of $D\times_P P'\to X\times_P P'$. Thus $V'$ represents the required locus after base change; its fibre-product identification with $V\times_P P'$ follows from the same universal property. The locus is unique since its point set is fixed by the residue-field tests. The empty base gives the empty locus; a rank-zero chart gives the whole chart; the tensor and determinant calculations never used reducedness or Noetherianity.

source.place: 01JP (definition-fibre-product); open-subscheme universal property, applied to the represented condition

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q98-c62659d83 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: PASS with no fixes. I read the whole item. The statement and stmt_deps are unchanged and there are no new nodes. The statement is true: on charts where B is free, the closed-immersion locus is D(Fit_0(B/im φ)), and Cayley–Hamilton makes im φ a finitely generated A-module, so Fit_0 has finitely many generators and the locus is a quasi-compact open. I checked each of the ten steps against the exact statements of the nodes it cites: lem-sc-finite-pushforward-locally-free, Cayley–Hamilton, tensor right exactness, the tilde module node, Fitting clause (1) at r=0 together with the stalk criterion (2) (checked at Stacks divisors.tex l.1352), the trf arbitrary-pullback and affine-sections nodes, the Leibniz determinant expansion, D(f)≅Spec A_f, spectrum compactness, affine fibre products, the affine closed-immersion criterion, and finite affine covers of quasi-compact opens. Each says what the step takes from it. Steps 9 and 10, which are local on the target and use universal properties, are genuinely elementary. Small cases check out: B=0; B=A×A with x↦(0,a) gives D(a), which is empty for a=ε over k[ε] and behaves correctly when ℤ is reduced to 𝔽₂ and 𝔽₃; m=0; P empty. No Noetherian, reduced or flat hypothesis is used. Batch-5 flags: lem-trf-fitting-ideal-generate-locally, lem-trf-fitting-sheaf-arbitrary-pullback and lem-trf-fitting-ideal-sheaf-affine-sections are generic Fitting-ideal algebra (Stacks 07Z6/0C3D/0C3F), outside both the trace formula and Poincaré duality, so all three are accepted. All four declared tool_uses are accepted as generic tools. The Conrad source is not local (already recorded as WANTED), and the proof is an agent-written Stacks route.
